expectations.text: The agent explains that IPublishedContentQueryAccessor only yields an IPublishedContentQuery during an HTTP request (it resolves from the request's services), which is why it works from a controller and returns false in the job
expectations.evidence: Lines 7-22 of response.md explain this precisely. The agent shows the simplified implementation of TryGetValue(), states 'From a controller: a request is running, so HttpContext exists' and 'From an IHostedService / timer / background job: no request is running, so HttpContext is null and TryGetValue returns false.'

expectations.text: The agent does not suggest keeping the accessor and retrying, or caching a query obtained during a request for later use by the job
expectations.evidence: The response does not suggest retrying the accessor or caching queries. Instead, lines 24-31 explicitly move toward proper solutions: using IRecurringBackgroundJob and either EnsureUmbracoContext or v15+ services. No mention of workarounds with the accessor.

expectations.text: The fix reads published content per run via IUmbracoContextFactory.EnsureUmbracoContext() inside a using (injecting the singleton IPublishedContentCache, available in Umbraco 15+, and looking up per call is equally acceptable)
expectations.evidence: Option A (lines 33-95) demonstrates EnsureUmbracoContext in a using statement (line 65). Option B (lines 107-147) demonstrates IPublishedContentCache for v15+ (line 116). Both approaches are correctly presented as alternatives.

expectations.text: Content is read from the published cache (UmbracoContext.Content and/or IDocumentNavigationQueryService), not from IContentService
expectations.evidence: Option A reads from UmbracoContext.Content (line 66). Option B uses IDocumentNavigationQueryService (lines 130-134) and IPublishedContentCache (line 139). Line 158 explicitly warns: 'Don't fall back to IContentService: it would work at night, but it reads from the database, returns drafts, and is slow.'

expectations.text: The agent notes that the docs' accessor advice applies to request-time code, not to background jobs
expectations.evidence: Line 24 directly addresses this: 'So the docs advice is only half right for your case. It is correct that you shouldn't read content through IContentService... But the accessor only covers request-bound code. Background code has to set up its own context.'

expectations.text: If no buildable project is available, the agent does not claim the fix was compiled or run
expectations.evidence: The agent qualifies the code as examples and notes: 'Check the exact method names against your 17.x version' (line 150). At the end, the agent states 'Sources (from memory of the Umbraco docs and source; check them against your exact 17.x version)' (lines 167-171), explicitly indicating no runtime verification.

eval_feedback.overall: All expectations are met with strong evidence. The agent correctly identifies the root cause (lack of HTTP request in background context), provides proper context on why the accessor pattern fails, and supplies two technically sound solutions with appropriate caveats. The answer qualifies its knowledge from memory and directs the user to verify against their specific version, which is appropriately cautious for a 17.x codebase. No weak assertions detected; the evaluation requirements align well with genuine technical understanding needed to solve this problem.
